description: Geographic computation and mapping: positions and distances on the Earth, map rendering with projections and backgrounds, thematic and statistical map plots, elevation and imagery data, and travel routing.

tools.name: GeoGraphics
tools.description: Renders a map, optionally with geographic primitives drawn on top of a chosen background such as street maps, satellite imagery or relief. The view range, projection and zoom level are all controllable. It is the foundation of all map output in the Wolfram Language.

parameters.name: GeoRange
parameters.description: Extent of the map: a distance, a country, or explicit latitude/longitude bounds.

parameters.name: GeoZoomLevel
parameters.description: Tile zoom level controlling detail of raster backgrounds.

tools.notes: Raster backgrounds require an internet connection; "VectorMinimal" works offline in most installations.

tools.name: GeoPosition
tools.description: Represents a location on the Earth by latitude and longitude, optionally with altitude and a datum. It is the canonical position object accepted by all geographic functions. Lists of positions are supported for efficiency.
tools.usage:
GeoPosition[{lat, lon}]
GeoPosition[{lat, lon, alt}]
GeoPosition[{p1, p2, ...}]
tools.notes: GeoGridPosition, GeoPositionXYZ and GeoPositionENU represent other coordinate systems.

tools.name: GeoDistance
tools.description: Computes the distance between two geographic locations along the surface of the Earth, using a geodesic on the reference ellipsoid by default. Results are Quantity objects with length units. It accepts positions, cities and other geographic entities.
tools.notes: GeoDistanceList gives the distances along a whole path.

tools.name: GeoDirection
tools.description: Gives the compass bearing from one geographic location to another, measured clockwise from north. It is the azimuth of the initial heading along the geodesic. Use it for navigation and antenna pointing.

tools.name: GeoDestination
tools.description: Finds the location reached by travelling a given distance in a given direction from a starting point. It is the inverse of GeoDistance and GeoDirection taken together. Use it for dead reckoning and for constructing offset points.

tools.name: GeoPath
tools.description: Represents a path between geographic locations, following a geodesic, rhumb line or great circle as specified. It draws correctly on any projection in GeoGraphics. Use it for routes, flight paths and connection maps.
tools.example:
GeoGraphics[{Thick, Red,
  GeoPath[{GeoPosition[{40.6, -73.8}], GeoPosition[{51.5, -0.5}]}, "Geodesic"]},
  GeoRange -> "World", GeoProjection -> "Robinson"]

tools.name: GeoCircle
tools.description: Represents a circle on the Earth's surface at a constant geodesic distance from a center. It appears as a closed curve correctly distorted by the projection. Use it for range rings, coverage limits and isochrones.

tools.name: GeoDisk
tools.description: Represents a filled disk on the Earth's surface centered at a location with a given geodesic radius. It is both a drawable primitive and a geographic region usable with GeoWithinQ. Use it for coverage areas and buffers.

tools.name: GeoMarker
tools.description: Draws a map marker at a geographic location, with a default pin graphic or a custom image. Lists of positions place many markers efficiently. Use it to pin points of interest on a map.

tools.name: GeoListPlot
tools.description: Plots a list of geographic locations or entities on a map, with automatic markers, labels and range selection. Groups of locations can be styled separately. Use it as the fastest way to map a set of places.

tools.name: GeoRegionValuePlot
tools.description: Draws a choropleth map, shading geographic regions according to associated numeric values. Regions can be countries, states, counties or any geographic entities. Use it for thematic maps of statistics such as population or income.

tools.name: GeoHistogram
tools.description: Bins geographic point data into cells on a map and shades them by count, the geographic analogue of a 2D histogram. Bin shape can be hexagonal, rectangular or based on administrative regions. Use it to show spatial density of events.

tools.name: GeoSmoothHistogram
tools.description: Produces a smooth kernel-density estimate of geographic point data drawn on a map. It avoids the blockiness of binned histograms. Use it for continuous density surfaces such as incident hotspots.

tools.name: GeoDensityPlot
tools.description: Plots a scalar function of latitude and longitude as a shaded density layer on a map. It is the geographic counterpart of DensityPlot. Use it for model outputs, interpolated fields and coverage predictions.
tools.notes: GeoContourPlot, GeoStreamPlot and GeoVectorPlot render contours and vector fields on maps.

tools.name: GeoContourPlot
tools.description: Draws contour lines of a scalar geographic field on a map. Values may come from a function of latitude and longitude or from scattered data. Use it for isotherms, isobars and elevation contours.

tools.name: GeoVectorPlot
tools.description: Draws a vector field on a map with arrows, for example wind or current data. Vectors can be specified as functions of position or as measured data. Use it for meteorological and oceanographic visualizations.
tools.notes: GeoStreamPlot draws streamlines instead of arrows.

tools.name: GeoBubbleChart
tools.description: Plots bubbles on a map whose size encodes a value associated with each location. It combines geographic placement with magnitude comparison. Use it for city populations, sales by region and similar data.

tools.name: GeoElevationData
tools.description: Retrieves terrain elevation data for a geographic region, returned as an array, image or GeoPosition data. Resolution can be requested explicitly. Use it for terrain analysis, relief rendering and line-of-sight computations.

tools.name: GeoImage
tools.description: Returns satellite or map imagery for a geographic region as an Image object. Zoom level and image size control the resolution. Use it when you want map tiles as pixels for image processing.

tools.name: GeoNearest
tools.description: Finds the geographic entities of a given type nearest to a location, such as the closest cities, airports or volcanoes. A count or a maximum distance limits the results. Use it for proximity lookups against the knowledgebase.
tools.usage:
GeoNearest[type, loc]
GeoNearest[type, loc, n]
GeoNearest[type, loc, dist]

tools.name: GeoWithinQ
tools.description: Tests whether a location lies inside a geographic region such as a country, disk or polygon. It returns True or False. Use it for point-in-region filtering of geographic datasets.

tools.name: GeoBounds
tools.description: Returns the latitude and longitude bounds of a geographic entity or set of locations. It is the geographic analogue of RegionBounds. Use it to size a map or to build a bounding query.
tools.notes: GeoBoundsRegion turns such bounds back into a region usable as GeoRange.

tools.name: GeoProjection
tools.description: Option specifying the map projection used to flatten the Earth onto the plane, with dozens of named projections and configurable parameters. The choice affects which of area, angle and distance are preserved. Set it explicitly for thematic maps where area distortion matters.

tools.name: GeoRange
tools.description: Option specifying the geographic extent shown on a map, given as a distance, a named region, an entity or explicit latitude and longitude bounds. It is the main way to frame a map. Automatic infers a range from the content being drawn.

tools.name: GeoBackground
tools.description: Option selecting the base layer of a map, such as street maps, satellite imagery, relief, vector outlines or a solid color. It determines both the look and whether an internet connection is needed. Combine it with GeoStyling for custom appearances.

tools.name: GeoPolygon
tools.description: Represents a polygon whose vertices are geographic positions, correctly drawn on any projection. It also serves as a geographic region for membership and area queries. Use it for administrative boundaries and custom zones.

tools.name: GeoLength
tools.description: Computes the length of a geographic path or the perimeter of a geographic region along the Earth's surface. The result is a Quantity with length units. Use it to measure routes, rivers and boundaries.
tools.notes: GeoArea gives the surface area of a geographic region.

tools.name: GeoArea
tools.description: Computes the area of a geographic region on the Earth's surface, accounting for its curvature. Results are Quantity objects with area units. Use it for land-area statistics and coverage computations.

tools.name: FindGeoLocation
tools.description: Estimates the current geographic location of the computer, typically from network information. It returns a GeoPosition. Use it to default maps and weather queries to the user's surroundings.
tools.notes: Accuracy depends on the network; $GeoLocation caches the value for the session.

tools.name: TravelDirections
tools.description: Computes routing directions between locations along roads or other travel modes, returning a TravelDirectionsData object with the route path, distance and time. The path can be drawn directly in GeoGraphics. Use it for logistics and trip planning.
tools.notes: Requires an internet connection and Wolfram service access.

tools.name: TravelDistance
tools.description: Gives the distance of a travel route between locations, following roads rather than the straight-line geodesic. TravelTime gives the estimated duration. Use it when actual travel effort matters more than map distance.
